Problem: PC in VLAN 10 cannot ping PC in VLAN 10 on adjacent switch.
Proposed Fix: Set switchport mode trunk on interconnecting interfaces.

Problem: Host on VLAN 20 cannot communicate with default gateway.
Root Cause: Access Port Assigned to Wrong VLAN
Proposed Fix: Reassign interface to VLAN 20 using switchport access vlan 20.

Problem: Switch port error-disabled due to port-security violation.
Proposed Fix: Clear sticky MAC settings and issue shutdown / no shutdown on port.

Problem: Trunk link down between Core and Access switches.
Proposed Fix: Align native VLAN IDs on both ends of trunk interface.

Problem: PC gets IP but cannot reach server in VLAN 30; gateway ping works.
Proposed Fix: Add ip route command or configure router-on-a-stick subinterfaces.

Problem: R1 cannot reach subnet on R2 across serial link.
Proposed Fix: Correct destination next-hop IP in static route table.

Problem: OSPF neighbor adjacencies failing to establish.
Proposed Fix: Align OSPF area IDs and timer intervals across neighboring routers.

Problem: High latency occurs when traffic passes across BGP peering link.
Proposed Fix: Adjust MED or Local Preference attributes for preferred routing.
Correction Reason: AI suggested resetting BGP peer; preferred adjusting Local Preference instead.

Problem: Router unable to forward packets to remote subnet 10.20.0.0/16.
Proposed Fix: Configure ip route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 pointing to ISP edge router.

Problem: Host receives APIPA address (169.254.x.x) on startup.
Root Cause: IP Configuration Error / DHCP Scope Mismatch
Proposed Fix: Reconfigure static IP setting or issue release/renew on host.

Problem: Branch PCs not receiving dynamic IP addresses from central server.
Root Cause: Missing IP Helper Address on Router Subinterface
Proposed Fix: Add ip helper-address <DHCP_SERVER_IP> to interface configuration.

Problem: DHCP pool exhausted on router, new clients failing connection.
Proposed Fix: Increase subnet pool scope size or lower DHCP lease timeouts.

Problem: PC can ping 8.8.8.8 but cannot browse websites by hostname.
Proposed Fix: Reconfigure primary and secondary DNS server IPs on host network config.

Problem: Internal clients failing to resolve local domain domain.local.
Proposed Fix: Flush client DNS cache and restart DNS service on domain controller.
Correction Reason: AI recommended changing DNS server; issue was resolved by clearing stale client cache.

Problem: Engineering workstation blocked from accessing FTP server.
Proposed Fix: Add explicit permit rule above deny rule in access list.

Problem: Guest Wi-Fi users able to access internal subnet 192.168.1.0/24.
Proposed Fix: Apply inbound ACL restricting access to private RFC 1918 addresses.

Problem: SSH access to router core-rtr-01 timing out from management PC.
Root Cause: VTY Line ACL Blocking IP Subnet
Proposed Fix: Update access-class on line vty 0 4 to include management IP.

Problem: Telnet blocked but SSH connection succeeds.
Root Cause: Explicit ACL Block on TCP Port 23
Proposed Fix: Normal security posture; no action required unless Telnet is explicitly needed.
Correction Reason: AI suggested enabling Telnet; rejected to maintain zero-trust security compliance.

Problem: Internal host 192.168.1.10 unreachable from internet.
Root Cause: Missing Static Port Forwarding / NAT Entry
Proposed Fix: Configure ip nat inside source static tcp for inbound traffic.

Problem: LAN hosts lose internet connectivity during peak usage hours.
Proposed Fix: Add additional public IPs to NAT pool dynamic allocation.

Problem: NAT interface overload failing to translate traffic.
Root Cause: NAT Outside / Inside Interface Configuration Inverted
Proposed Fix: Verify ip nat inside and ip nat outside directives on router interfaces.
Correction Reason: AI suggested restarting NAT service; corrected interface assignment tags.

Problem: Laptop cannot connect to enterprise Wi-Fi network SSID Corp-Wifi.
Proposed Fix: Verify RADIUS server shared secret key and user credentials.

Problem: Wireless clients disconnecting periodically in conference room.
Root Cause: RF Co-Channel Interference / High Noise Floor
Proposed Fix: Adjust AP channel power assignment and switch to non-overlapping channels.

Problem: IoT devices failing to connect to 5GHz wireless access point.
Proposed Fix: Enable 2.4GHz radio band broadcast on designated SSID.

Problem: Port speed mismatch detected between Core Switch and Server 01.
Proposed Fix: Set speed/duplex to auto-negotiate or configure matching parameters.

Problem: Interface FastEthernet0/1 goes up and down constantly (flapping).
Proposed Fix: Replace Ethernet patch cable or optic SFP module.

Problem: Switch port stuck in err-disabled state after loop detected.
Root Cause: BPDU Guard Triggered by Unmanaged Switch
Proposed Fix: Remove unauthorized device and re-enable port with shutdown/no shutdown.

Problem: High CPU utilization on core switch (over 98%).
Root Cause: Broadcast Storm / Spanning Tree Protocol Loop
Proposed Fix: Verify STP topologies and configure PortFast / BPDU Filter correctly.
Correction Reason: AI suggested rebooting core switch; resolved STP loop manually to avoid downtime.

Problem: Router interface line protocol is down, signal state is up.
Proposed Fix: Verify serial encapsulation type (HDLC/PPP) on both endpoints.

Problem: VPN tunnel between site A and site B failing Phase 2 negotiation.
Root Cause: IPsec Transform Set / Traffic Selector Mismatch
Proposed Fix: Align Phase 2 IPsec transform sets and crypto map ACLs.
Correction Reason: AI recommended rebuilding tunnel from scratch; resolved by updating ACL matching rules.

Problem: PC0 cannot ping PC1. Both host devices are connected to Switch0.
Root Cause: One or both of the switch ports connected to PC0 and PC1 are administratively shut down, preventing any Layer 1 or Layer 2 communication.
Next Command:
show interface status
show interface <PC0_port>
show interface <PC1_port>
Proposed Fix:
Identify the switch ports connecting to PC0 and PC1. If their status is 'administratively down', enable them using the 'no shutdown' command in interface configuration mode:

configure terminal
interface <PC0_port_name>
  no shutdown
exit
interface <PC1_port_name>
  no shutdown
exit

Replace `<PC0_port_name>` and `<PC1_port_name>` with the actual interface names (e.g., `GigabitEthernet0/1`).
Correction Reason: Approved configuration. Verified that VLAN isolation on ports Fa0/1 and Fa0/2 was the root cause and the suggested fix is safe to apply.

Root Cause: PC0 and PC1 are likely assigned to different VLANs on Switch0, preventing direct Layer 2 communication.
Proposed Fix: First, identify the specific switch ports to which PC0 and PC1 are connected. If they are in different VLANs and intended to communicate directly at Layer 2, configure both access ports to belong to the same VLAN. For example, if PC0 is connected to Fa0/1 (VLAN 10) and PC1 is connected to Fa0/2 (VLAN 20), and they should both be in VLAN 10: `configure terminal` `interface Fa0/2` `switchport access vlan 10` `end`
Correction Reason: Approved configuration. Verified that VLAN isolation on ports Fa0/1 and Fa0/2 was the root cause and the suggested fix is safe to apply.
